question: What is the default router mode in Docsify, and what does a URL look like in that mode?
answer:
# Default Router Mode in Docsify

## Hash Routing as the Default

[Data: Entities (2454)]

Hash routing is the default routing mode in Docsify. This means that by default, Docsify uses the hash symbol (#) in URLs for client-side navigation.

## URL Structure in Hash Routing Mode

In hash routing mode, URLs incorporate the hash symbol to denote different pages and routes within the documentation site. For example, a URL may look like `http://domain.com/#/guide`, where the hash symbol separates the base domain from the route path. This approach allows Docsify to handle navigation entirely on the client side without requiring server-side routing configuration.

The documentation recommends starting with hash routing as the default option. If you want to explore alternative routing modes, you can switch to history mode for a better user experience without the `#` in the URL and improved SEO optimization, though this requires additional server configuration [Data: Sources (156)].

docsify
========================

> A magical documentation site generator.

What it is
------------------------------

Docsify turns your Markdown files into a documentation website instantly. Unlike most other documentation site generator tools, it doesn't need to build HTML files. Instead, it dynamically loads and parses your Markdown files and displays them as a website. To get started, create an `index.html` file and [deploy it on GitHub Pages](#/deploy) (for more details see the [Quick start](#/quickstart) guide).

Features
--------------------------

* No statically built HTML files
* Simple and lightweight
* Smart full-text search plugin
* Multiple themes
* Useful plugin API
* Emoji support

Examples
--------------------------

Check out the [Showcase](https://github.com/docsifyjs/awesome-docsify#showcase) to see docsify in use.

Donate
----------------------

Please consider donating if you think docsify is helpful to you or that my work is valuable. I am happy if you can help me [buy a cup of coffee](https://github.com/QingWei-Li/donate).

Community
----------------------------

Users and the development team are usually in the [Discord server](https://discord.gg/3NwKFyR).

---

Adding pages
==============================================

If you need more pages, you can simply create more markdown files in your docsify directory. If you create a file named `guide.md`, then it is accessible via `/#/guide`.

For example, the directory structure is as follows:

```
.
└── docs
    ├── README.md
    ├── guide.md
    └── zh-cn
        ├── README.md
        └── guide.md
```

Matching routes

```
docs/README.md        => http://domain.com
docs/guide.md         => http://domain.com/#/guide
docs/zh-cn/README.md  => http://domain.com/#/zh-cn/
docs/zh-cn/guide.md   => http://domain.com/#/zh-cn/guide
```

Sidebar
------------------------------------

In order to have a sidebar, you can create your own `_sidebar.md` (see [this documentation's sidebar](https://github.com/docsifyjs/docsify/blob/main/docs/_sidebar.md) for an example):

First, you need to set `loadSidebar` to **true**. Details are available in the [configuration paragraph](#/configuration?id=loadsidebar).

```
<!-- index.html -->

<script>
  window.$docsify = {
    loadSidebar: true,
  };
</script>
<script src="//cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/docsify@5/dist/docsify.min.js"></script>
```

Create the `_sidebar.md`:

```
<!-- docs/_sidebar.md -->

- [Home](/)
- [Page 1](page-1.md)
```

To create section headers:

```
<!-- docs/_sidebar.md -->

- Section Header 1

  - [Home](/)
  - [Page 1](page-1.md)

- Section Header 2

  - [Page 2](page-2.md)
  - [Page 3](page-3.md)
```

You need to create a `.nojekyll` in `./docs` to prevent GitHub Pages from ignoring files that begin with an underscore.

Docsify only looks for `_sidebar.md` in the current folder, and uses that, otherwise it falls back to the one configured using `window.$docsify.loadSidebar` config.

Example file structure:

```
└── docs/
    ├── _sidebar.md
    ├── index.md
    ├── getting-started.md
    └── running-services.md
```

Nested Sidebars
----------------------------------------------------

You may want the sidebar to update after navigation to reflect the current directory. This can be done by adding a `_sidebar.md` file to each folder.

`_sidebar.md` is loaded from each level directory. If the current directory doesn't have `_sidebar.md`, it will fall back to the parent directory. If, for example, the current path is `/guide/quick-start`, the `_sidebar.md` will be loaded from `/guide/_sidebar.md`.

You can specify `alias` to avoid unnecessary fallback.

```
<script>
  window.$docsify = {
    loadSidebar: true,
    alias: {
      '/.*/_sidebar.md': '/_sidebar.md',
    },
  };
</script>
```

You can create a `README.md` file in a subdirectory to use it as the landing page for the route.

Set Page Titles from Sidebar Selection
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

A page's `title` tag is generated from the *selected* sidebar item name. For better SEO, you can customize the title by specifying a string after the filename.

```
<!-- docs/_sidebar.md -->

- [Home](/)
- [Guide](guide.md 'The greatest guide in the world')
```

Table of Contents
--------------------------------------------------------

Once you've created `_sidebar.md`, the sidebar content is automatically generated based on the headers in the markdown files.

A custom sidebar can also automatically generate a table of contents by setting a `subMaxLevel`, compare [subMaxLevel configuration](#/configuration?id=submaxlevel).

```
<!-- index.html -->

<script>
  window.$docsify = {
    loadSidebar: true,
    subMaxLevel: 2,
  };
</script>
<script src="//cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/docsify@5/dist/docsify.min.js"></script>
```

Ignoring Subheaders
------------------------------------------------------------

When `subMaxLevel` is set, each header is automatically added to the table of contents by default. If you want to ignore a specific header, add `<!-- {docsify-ignore} -->` to it.

```
# Getting Started

## Header <!-- {docsify-ignore} -->

This header won't appear in the sidebar table of contents.
```

To ignore all headers on a specific page, you can use `<!-- {docsify-ignore-all} -->` on the first header of the page.

```
# Getting Started <!-- {docsify-ignore-all} -->

## Header

This header won't appear in the sidebar table of contents.
```

Both `<!-- {docsify-ignore} -->` and `<!-- {docsify-ignore-all} -->` will not be rendered on the page when used.

And the `{docsify-ignore}` and `{docsify-ignore-all}` can do the samething as well.

question: How do I hide a single header from the Docsify sidebar table of contents, and how do I hide all headers on a page?
answer:
# Hiding Headers from the Docsify Sidebar

Docsify provides two HTML comment tags that allow you to control which headers appear in the sidebar table of contents.

## Hiding a Single Header

To hide a specific header from the sidebar table of contents, add the `<!-- {docsify-ignore} -->` comment tag directly after the header text [Data: Sources (149)]. For example:

```markdown
# Getting Started

## Header <!-- {docsify-ignore} -->

This header won't appear in the sidebar table of contents.
```

The header will still be rendered on the page itself, but it will be excluded from the sidebar navigation [Data: Sources (149)].

## Hiding All Headers on a Page

To exclude all headers on a specific page from appearing in the sidebar table of contents, use the `<!-- {docsify-ignore-all} -->` comment tag on the first header of the page [Data: Sources (149)]. Here's an example:

```markdown
# Getting Started <!-- {docsify-ignore-all} -->

## Header

This header won't appear in the sidebar table of contents.
```

Like the single-header ignore tag, this comment will not be rendered on the page when used [Data: Sources (149)].

## Important Note

Both `<!-- {docsify-ignore} -->` and `<!-- {docsify-ignore-all} -->` tags function as HTML comments and will not appear in the rendered output on your page [Data: Sources (149)]. Additionally, you can use the alternative syntax `{docsify-ignore}` and `{docsify-ignore-all}` (without the HTML comment delimiters) to achieve the same results [Data: Sources (149)].

question: What are the lifecycle hooks available to a Docsify plugin, and which of them run on every page load?
answer:
# Docsify Plugin Lifecycle Hooks

Docsify plugins have access to several lifecycle hooks that allow developers to execute custom JavaScript code at various stages of the framework's operation [Data: Entities (2476); Sources (158)].

## Available Lifecycle Hooks

The complete set of lifecycle hooks available to Docsify plugins includes:

1. **init()** - Invoked one time when the docsify script is initialized [Data: Sources (158)]
2. **mounted()** - Invoked one time when the docsify instance has mounted on the DOM [Data: Entities (2479); Sources (158)]
3. **beforeEach()** - Invoked on each page load before new markdown is transformed to HTML [Data: Sources (158)]
4. **afterEach()** - Invoked on each page load after new markdown has been transformed to HTML [Data: Sources (158)]
5. **doneEach()** - Invoked on each page load after new HTML has been appended to the DOM [Data: Sources (158)]
6. **ready()** - Invoked one time after rendering the initial page [Data: Sources (158)]

## Hooks That Run on Every Page Load

Three of these lifecycle hooks execute on every page load:

- **beforeEach()** runs before markdown is converted to HTML on each page load
- **afterEach()** runs after markdown has been transformed to HTML on each page load
- **doneEach()** runs after the new HTML has been appended to the DOM on each page load

In contrast, the **init()**, **mounted()**, and **ready()** hooks each execute only once during the plugin's lifetime [Data: Sources (158)].

## Important Considerations for Asynchronous Code

When using asynchronous tasks in hooks like **beforeEach()** and **afterEach()**, it is recommended to wrap the code in a try/catch/finally block to prevent errors from affecting Docsify and other plugins [Data: Entities (2493); Sources (158)].

question: What is the default value of Docsify's maxLevel option, and what does it control?
answer:
# Docsify's maxLevel Configuration Option

## Default Value and Purpose

The `maxLevel` configuration option in Docsify has a default value of 6 [Data: Sources (152); Entities (2390)]. This option controls the maximum heading level that will be displayed in the Table of Contents [Data: Sources (152); Entities (2390)].

## How It Works

When you configure `maxLevel`, you are setting a limit on the depth of headers that Docsify will include when automatically generating the table of contents. With the default value of 6, the Table of Contents will include headings up to the sixth level of hierarchy [Data: Entities (2390)].

## Configuration

The `maxLevel` option is defined within the `window.$docsify` global configuration object [Data: Relationships (3637)]. You can customize this setting by modifying it in your configuration:

```javascript
window.$docsify = {
  maxLevel: 4,
};
```

This example would limit the table of contents to display only headings up to the fourth level, reducing the depth and granularity of the generated table of contents structure [Data: Sources (152)].

contexts.text:
Adding pages
==============================================

If you need more pages, you can simply create more markdown files in your docsify directory. If you create a file named `guide.md`, then it is accessible via `/#/guide`.

For example, the directory structure is as follows:

```
.
└── docs
    ├── README.md
    ├── guide.md
    └── zh-cn
        ├── README.md
        └── guide.md
```

Matching routes

```
docs/README.md        => http://domain.com
docs/guide.md         => http://domain.com/#/guide
docs/zh-cn/README.md  => http://domain.com/#/zh-cn/
docs/zh-cn/guide.md   => http://domain.com/#/zh-cn/guide
```

Sidebar
------------------------------------

In order to have a sidebar, you can create your own `_sidebar.md` (see [this documentation's sidebar](https://github.com/docsifyjs/docsify/blob/main/docs/_sidebar.md) for an example):

First, you need to set `loadSidebar` to **true**. Details are available in the [configuration paragraph](#/configuration?id=loadsidebar).

```
<!-- index.html -->

<script>
  window.$docsify = {
    loadSidebar: true,
  };
</script>
<script src="//cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/docsify@5/dist/docsify.min.js"></script>
```

Create the `_sidebar.md`:

```
<!-- docs/_sidebar.md -->

- [Home](/)
- [Page 1](page-1.md)
```

To create section headers:

```
<!-- docs/_sidebar.md -->

- Section Header 1

  - [Home](/)
  - [Page 1](page-1.md)

- Section Header 2

  - [Page 2](page-2.md)
  - [Page 3](page-3.md)
```

You need to create a `.nojekyll` in `./docs` to prevent GitHub Pages from ignoring files that begin with an underscore.

Docsify only looks for `_sidebar.md` in the current folder, and uses that, otherwise it falls back to the one configured using `window.$docsify.loadSidebar` config.

Example file structure:

```
└── docs/
    ├── _sidebar.md
    ├── index.md
    ├── getting-started.md
    └── running-services.md
```

Nested Sidebars
----------------------------------------------------

You may want the sidebar to update after navigation to reflect the current directory. This can be done by adding a `_sidebar.md` file to each folder.

`_sidebar.md` is loaded from each level directory. If the current directory doesn't have `_sidebar.md`, it will fall back to the parent directory. If, for example, the current path is `/guide/quick-start`, the `_sidebar.md` will be loaded from `/guide/_sidebar.md`.

You can specify `alias` to avoid unnecessary fallback.

```
<script>
  window.$docsify = {
    loadSidebar: true,
    alias: {
      '/.*/_sidebar.md': '/_sidebar.md',
    },
  };
</script>
```

You can create a `README.md` file in a subdirectory to use it as the landing page for the route.

Set Page Titles from Sidebar Selection
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

A page's `title` tag is generated from the *selected* sidebar item name. For better SEO, you can customize the title by specifying a string after the filename.

```
<!-- docs/_sidebar.md -->

- [Home](/)
- [Guide](guide.md 'The greatest guide in the world')
```

Table of Contents
--------------------------------------------------------

Once you've created `_sidebar.md`, the sidebar content is automatically generated based on the headers in the markdown files.

A custom sidebar can also automatically generate a table of contents by setting a `subMaxLevel`, compare [subMaxLevel configuration](#/configuration?id=submaxlevel).

```
<!-- index.html -->

<script>
  window.$docsify = {
    loadSidebar: true,
    subMaxLevel: 2,
  };
</script>
<script src="//cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/docsify@5/dist/docsify.min.js"></script>
```

Ignoring Subheaders
------------------------------------------------------------

When `subMaxLevel` is set, each header is automatically added to the table of contents by default. If you want to ignore a specific header, add `<!-- {docsify-ignore} -->` to it.

```
# Getting Started

## Header <!-- {docsify-ignore} -->

This header won't appear in the sidebar table of contents.
```

To ignore all headers on a specific page, you can use `<!-- {docsify-ignore-all} -->` on the first header of the page.

```
# Getting Started <!-- {docsify-ignore-all} -->

## Header

This header won't appear in the sidebar table of contents.
```

Both `<!-- {docsify-ignore} -->` and `<!-- {docsify-ignore-all} -->` will not be rendered on the page when used.

And the `{docsify-ignore}` and `{docsify-ignore-all}` can do the samething as well.

question: How do I make Docsify show a custom 404 page?
answer:
# Custom 404 Page in Docsify

To display a custom 404 page in Docsify, you need to create a `_404.md` file in your documentation directory. [Data: Entities (2447)]

## Implementation

When a user navigates to a page that doesn't exist, Docsify will load and display the content from your `_404.md` file instead of showing a default error message. This allows you to customize the appearance and messaging of your 404 error page to match your documentation site's design and provide helpful information to users.

You can create this file just like any other markdown file in your docs folder, and style it with custom content, links back to your main documentation, or suggestions for what users might have been looking for.

docsify

> A magical documentation site generator.

What it is
------------------------------

Docsify turns your Markdown files into a documentation website instantly. Unlike most other documentation site generator tools, it doesn't need to build HTML files. Instead, it dynamically loads and parses your Markdown files and displays them as a website. To get started, create an `index.html` file and [deploy it on GitHub Pages](#/deploy) (for more details see the [Quick start](#/quickstart) guide).

Features
--------------------------

* No statically built HTML files
* Simple and lightweight
* Smart full-text search plugin
* Multiple themes
* Useful plugin API
* Emoji support

Examples
--------------------------

Check out the [Showcase](https://github.com/docsifyjs/awesome-docsify#showcase) to see docsify in use.

Donate

Community
----------------------------

---

Embed files
===========================================

With docsify 4.6 it is now possible to embed any type of file.

You can embed these files as video, audio, iframes, or code blocks, and even Markdown files can even be embedded directly into the document.

For example, here is an embedded Markdown file. You only need to do this:

```
[filename](_media/example.md ':include')
```

Then the content of `example.md` will be displayed directly here:

> This is from the `example.md`

You can check the original content for [example.md](_media/example.md).

Normally, this will be compiled into a link, but in docsify, if you add `:include` it will be embedded. You can use single or double quotation marks around as you like.

External links can be used too - just replace the target. If you want to use a gist URL, see [Embed a gist](#/embed-files?id=embed-a-gist) section.

Embedded file type
---------------------------------------------------------

Currently, file extensions are automatically recognized and embedded in different ways.

These types are supported:

* **iframe** `.html`, `.htm`
* **markdown** `.markdown`, `.md`
* **audio** `.mp3`
* **video** `.mp4`, `.ogg`
* **code** other file extension

Of course, you can force the specified type. For example, a Markdown file can be embedded as a code block by setting `:type=code`.

```
[filename](_media/example.md ':include :type=code')
```

You will get:

```
> This is from the `example.md`
```

Markdown with YAML Front Matter
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Front Matter, commonly utilized in blogging systems like Jekyll, serves to define metadata for a document. The [front-matter.js](https://www.npmjs.com/package/front-matter) package facilitates the extraction of metadata (front matter) from documents.

When using Markdown, YAML front matter will be stripped from the rendered content. The attributes cannot be used in this case.

```
<script src="//cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/docsify@5/dist/plugins/front-matter.min.js"></script>
```

```
[filename](_media/example-with-yaml.md ':include')
```

You will get just the content

> This is from the `example-with-yaml.md`

Embedded code fragments
-------------------------------------------------------------------

Sometimes you don't want to embed a whole file. Maybe because you need just a few lines but you want to compile and test the file in CI.

```
[filename](_media/example.js ':include :type=code :fragment=demo')
```

In your code file you need to surround the fragment between `/// [demo]` lines (before and after the fragment).
Alternatively you can use `### [demo]`. By default, only identifiers are omitted. To omit the entire line containing the identifier in the fragment output, add the `:omitFragmentLine` option. This is useful if your code fragment is e.g. HTML and you want to hide the Docsify fragment identifier from showing in your HTML source. `<!-- /// [demo] -->` in your source file and `:omitFragmentLine` will make the `-->` not show up in your Docsify code fragment section.

Example: In the source file \_media/example.js, `/// [demo]` identifiers have been included:

```
[filename](_media/example.js ':include :type=code')
```

```
import fetch from 'fetch';

const URL = 'https://example.com';
const PORT = 8080;

/// [demo]
const result = fetch(`${URL}:${PORT}`)
  .then(response => {
    return response.json();
  })
  .then(myJson => {
    console.log(JSON.stringify(myJson));
  });
/// [demo]

result.then(console.log).catch(console.error);
```

Adding the `:fragment=demo` results in the following:

```
[filename](_media/example.js ':include :type=code :fragment=demo')
```

```

  .then(response => {
    return response.json();
  })
  .then(myJson => {
    console.log(JSON.stringify(myJson));
  });
```

Tag attribute
-----------------------------------------------

If you embed the file as `iframe`, `audio` and `video`, then you may need to set the attributes of these tags.

Note, for the `audio` and `video` types, docsify adds the `controls` attribute by default. When you want add more attributes, the `controls` attribute need to be added manually if need be.

question: I want a cover page that is shown alone on the home page, with a separate markdown navbar. Which Docsify options and files do I need?
answer:
# Setting Up a Cover Page with Separate Navbar in Docsify

To achieve a cover page displayed alone on the home page with a separate markdown-based navbar, you'll need to configure specific Docsify options and create particular files.

## Required Configuration Options

You need to set two key configuration options in your `window.$docsify` object [Data: Sources (150, 152); Entities (2359); Relationships (3595, 3599)]:

1. **`coverpage`** - Set this to `true` to activate the cover feature. This will load from the default `_coverpage.md` file by default [Data: Entities (2359); Relationships (3596)].

2. **`onlyCover`** - This option controls whether the coverpage appears separately from the homepage. You'll want to enable this to ensure the cover page appears alone on the home page [Data: Relationships (3599)].

3. **`loadNavbar`** - Set this to `true` to load navbar configuration from the `_navbar.md` file [Data: Entities (2372); Relationships (3611)].

Your configuration should look like this:

```javascript
window.$docsify = {
  coverpage: true,
  onlyCover: true,
  loadNavbar: true,
};
```

## Required Files

You'll need to create two markdown files:

1. **`_coverpage.md`** - This file contains your cover page content and is automatically loaded when the `coverpage` option is enabled [Data: Entities (2360); Relationships (3596)]. The cover page can be customized using theme properties for styling [Data: Relationships (3605)].

2. **`_navbar.md`** - This file defines your navigation bar structure using markdown syntax [Data: Entities (2372); Relationships (3611)]. You can create nested menus and organize navigation links hierarchically [Data: Sources (151)].

## Important Note for GitHub Pages

If you're deploying to GitHub Pages, you must create a `.nojekyll` file in your docs directory to prevent GitHub Pages from ignoring files that begin with an underscore [Data: Relationships (3613)].

  - [Page 1](page-1.md)

- Section Header 2

  - [Page 2](page-2.md)
  - [Page 3](page-3.md)
```

You need to create a `.nojekyll` in `./docs` to prevent GitHub Pages from ignoring files that begin with an underscore.

Docsify only looks for `_sidebar.md` in the current folder, and uses that, otherwise it falls back to the one configured using `window.$docsify.loadSidebar` config.

Example file structure:

```
└── docs/
    ├── _sidebar.md
    ├── index.md
    ├── getting-started.md
    └── running-services.md
```

Nested Sidebars
----------------------------------------------------

You may want the sidebar to update after navigation to reflect the current directory. This can be done by adding a `_sidebar.md` file to each folder.

`_sidebar.md` is loaded from each level directory. If the current directory doesn't have `_sidebar.md`, it will fall back to the parent directory. If, for example, the current path is `/guide/quick-start`, the `_sidebar.md` will be loaded from `/guide/_sidebar.md`.

You can specify `alias` to avoid unnecessary fallback.

```
<script>
  window.$docsify = {
    loadSidebar: true,
    alias: {
      '/.*/_sidebar.md': '/_sidebar.md',
    },
  };
</script>
```

You can create a `README.md` file in a subdirectory to use it as the landing page for the route.

Set Page Titles from Sidebar Selection
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

A page's `title` tag is generated from the *selected* sidebar item name. For better SEO, you can customize the title by specifying a string after the filename.

```
<!-- docs/_sidebar.md -->

- [Home](/)
- [Guide](guide.md 'The greatest guide in the world')
```

Table of Contents
--------------------------------------------------------

Once you've created `_sidebar.md`, the sidebar content is automatically generated based on the headers in the markdown files.

A custom sidebar can also automatically generate a table of contents by setting a `subMaxLevel`, compare [subMaxLevel configuration](#/configuration?id=submaxlevel).

```
<!-- index.html -->

<script>
  window.$docsify = {
    loadSidebar: true,
    subMaxLevel: 2,
  };
</script>
<script src="//cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/docsify@5/dist/docsify.min.js"></script>
```

Ignoring Subheaders
------------------------------------------------------------

When `subMaxLevel` is set, each header is automatically added to the table of contents by default. If you want to ignore a specific header, add `<!-- {docsify-ignore} -->` to it.

```
# Getting Started

## Header <!-- {docsify-ignore} -->

This header won't appear in the sidebar table of contents.
```

To ignore all headers on a specific page, you can use `<!-- {docsify-ignore-all} -->` on the first header of the page.

```
# Getting Started <!-- {docsify-ignore-all} -->

## Header

This header won't appear in the sidebar table of contents.
```

Both `<!-- {docsify-ignore} -->` and `<!-- {docsify-ignore-all} -->` will not be rendered on the page when used.

And the `{docsify-ignore}` and `{docsify-ignore-all}` can do the samething as well.

---

Cover
=========================

Activate the cover feature by setting `coverpage` to **true**. See [coverpage configuration](#/configuration?id=coverpage).

Basic usage
-------------------------------------

Set `coverpage` to **true**, and create a `_coverpage.md`:

```
window.$docsify = {
  coverpage: true,
};
```

```
<!-- _coverpage.md -->

# docsify

> A magical documentation site generator

- Simple and lightweight
- No statically built HTML files
- Multiple themes

[GitHub](https://github.com/docsifyjs/docsify/)
Get Started
```

-----------------------------------------

The cover page can be customized using [theme properties](#/themes?id=theme-properties):

```

  --cover-bg         : url('path/to/image.png');
  --cover-bg-overlay : rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.5);
  --cover-color      : #fff;

  --cover-title-font : 600 var(--font-size-xxxl) var(--font-family);
}
```

```
<!-- background color -->

```

```
<!-- background image -->

```

Normally, the coverpage and the homepage appear at the same time. Of course, you can also separate the coverpage by [`onlyCover`](#/configuration?id=onlycover) option.

## Using `go get` Command

The primary method to install go-echarts v2 with Go modules is to use the `go get` command. You can install the package directly from the GitHub repository with the following command [Data: Sources (132)]:

```
$ go get -u github.com/go-echarts/go-echarts/v2/...
```

## Using go.mod File

Alternatively, you can specify go-echarts as a dependency directly in your project's `go.mod` file [Data: Sources (132)]:

```
# go.mod

require github.com/go-echarts/go-echarts/v2
```

After adding this line to your `go.mod` file, running `go mod download` or building your project will automatically fetch the package.

It's important to note that V2 is incompatible with V1, so if you're upgrading from an earlier version, you cannot smoothly upgrade and may need to make adjustments to your code [Data: Entities (2061); Relationships (3120)].

Summary ======================================= go-echarts is a golang lib providing the power to create [echarts](https://echarts.apache.org/) styling charts in go. --- What go-echarts does ================================================================= * Provide the generic HTML templates with echarts resources. * Generate echarts required options and datasets based on go programs. * Mount options to echarts' instance and render all in one place. --- What go-echarts changes and provide =============================================================================================== Option Types ------------------------------------------------- echarts is a pure JS lib which provides lots of flexible abilities on types and functions. In golang, go-echarts is not feasible to achieve it in a simple way. Besides, some of the options may have default values which may not consistent with go types. Therefore, we change some types following this guideline for now: * If the bool option with default(missing) value `(true)`, define it `*bool`(`types.Bool`) and provide the handy func `opts.Bool()` to do convert easily. * If the option is `string|string array` or `number|number array`, define it in `type array` or `interface{}`. * If the option is a complex struct, define it `interface{}` or providing an usable function, convert it then. JS Function and Formatter String ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- > Formatter string sounds like a DSL for echarts, such as `formatter: '{b0}: {c0}
{b1}: {c1}'` or a pure JS > function. Since go-echarts renders the options to charts pure in go, there is no way to apply JS functions either on echarts options or echarts instance directly. Instead, we provide the ability to insert pure JS function string and some useful functional wrapper api to help users do operations on echarts and echarts instance. The type of those kind of `Function String` is `types.FuncStr`. *When you find the option type is `types.FuncStr`, you should notice it. :)* How to insert the pure JS function --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- * Use `opts.FuncOpts` or `opts.FuncStripCommentsOpts` to create your JS string. * Use `myChart.AddJSFuncStrs()` to add the JS function into your charts. For example: ``` actionWithEchartsInstance := ` let currentIndex = -1; setInterval(function() { const myChart = %MY_ECHARTS%; var dataLen = myChart.getOption().series[0].data.length; myChart.dispatchAction({ type: 'downplay', seriesIndex: 0, dataIndex: currentIndex }); currentIndex = (currentIndex + 1) % dataLen; myChart.dispatchAction({ type: 'highlight', seriesIndex: 0, dataIndex: currentIndex }); myChart.dispatchAction({ type: 'showTip', seriesIndex: 0, dataIndex: currentIndex }); }, 1000); ` pie := charts.NewPie() pie.AddJSFuncStrs(opts.FuncOpts(actionWithEchartsInstance) ``` > BTW: use `const` to define a pure function string can do the builtin convert directly. How to get echarts instance ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Especially, you may notice the special var `%MY_ECHARTS%` in the example above. The `%MY_ECHARTS%` is the placeholder of the `echarts instance` in go-echarts. It will inject each of the real `echarts instance` of the chart into your functions. We believe it could bring more convenient to you when you want to do some advance operates on charts. Normally, you don't need it when you don't need do functions on chart, since go-echarts wants keep it always simple. --- Where to find options you need ===================================================================================== go-echarts' options are almost align to [echarts' official options](https://echarts.apache.org/en/option.html#title). If you want to find the options of your specific charts, all in the echarts options list. And if you find some options go-echarts hasn't supported yet, kindly create a PR or raise an option request. --- Where to find custom echarts resources ===================================================================================================== Currently, we support echarts' version is `v5.4.3` and the compatible version `v4.3` for those 3d charts and customized charts, such as word-cloud. All the resources are hosted in [go-echarts-assets](https://github.com/go-echarts/go-echarts-assets) by go-echarts itself. If you want to use your custom echarts resources. You could find in the [jsdelivr of echarts](https://www.jsdelivr.com/package/npm/echarts) or other CDN providers. Besides, you can set your own assets host as well. We support 2 ways to customize the echarts resources. * Only change the `Asserts Host`, which needs the echarts resources naming `echarts.min.js` * Clean all the preset assets and add custom resources all by yourself. ---

Ecosystem of go-echarts
=======================================================================

Welcome to contribute your awesome integration case !!!

This part lists all the ecosystem of go-echarts. Thanks for those great works.

* [`templ`](https://github.com/a-h/templ) A language for writing HTML user interfaces in Go. You can use `go-echarts` as its components.
* [`GoNB`](https://github.com/janpfeifer/gonb) A Go Notebook Kernel for Jupyter. You can run `go-echarts` inside of it smoothly, see [examples](https://janpfeifer.github.io/gonb-echarts/).
* [`insyra`](https://github.com/HazelnutParadise/insyra) A next-generation data analysis library for Golang(`go-echarts` as the main visualization backend).

---

Container of echarts
=======================================================================

A `Container` is used to define a root dom box of echarts instance and how to render charts.
It contains the height, width...etc, more
in [echarts Chart Container](https://echarts.apache.org/handbook/en/concepts/chart-size)

It focuses on the single echarts box instead of the whole pages,
go-echarts follows its rules on each chart level as well.
Obviously, go-echarts needs the HTML page management thing before do echarts stuff also.

Container of go-echarts
=============================================================================

In go-echarts, there have two approaches to manage charts, for single chart and for multi charts.
It has a little different points more than a simple aggregation operation either.
The `Container` is more close to a `HTML` page result in go-echarts.

* On single chart, it only has the single Chart Container with Chart Render.
* On multi charts, it only has the single Page Container with Page Render.

**There is no strict `1:n` relationship between `Chart Container` and `Page Container`.**

We hold the `Charter` (interface for charts) instances in program level for `Chart Container` and `Page Container`
with individual templates.

Chart Container
-------------------------------------------------------------

A Chart Container is made for a single chart.
The templates it required:

* header.tpl
* base.tpl
* chart.tpl

It allows to customize the asserts on JS and CSS, and provides the shortcuts for page settings.
Because it is only one chart which means it is associated with single echarts container also.
Any change only applies to the single chart page, directly and plain.

Page Container
-----------------------------------------------------------

A Page Container is made for multi charts.
The templates it required:

* header.tpl
* base.tpl
* page.tpl

It allows to customize the assets on JS and CSS on page level and charts level.
Because it contains multi charts in one page, it is associated with multi echarts containers also.
There support layout types:

* 'none'
* 'center'
* 'flex'

Any changes on page level should compatible to chart level, otherwise, it may has side effect.

**Attention**

* In `Page Container`, all the config for page related options on chart level will be ignored, such as `PageTitile`.
* If you want to reset Page assets entirely, only clear preset assets on page level might not work,since the charts level's preset assets
  will replenish it。you need clear all the page assets related options in both Page and Charts level.

---

question: Can I upgrade a go-echarts v1 project to v2 directly?
answer:
# Upgrading from Go-Echarts V1 to V2

## Direct Upgrade Not Possible

No, you cannot upgrade a go-echarts v1 project to v2 directly. [Data: Entities (2061, 2060); Relationships (3120)] V1 and V2 are fundamentally incompatible versions, which means that a smooth upgrade path does not exist between them.

## What This Means for Your Project

If you are currently using v1 and want to migrate to v2, you will need to make adjustments to your codebase. While the upgrade is not smooth, the go-echarts team believes the new version is worth the effort to migrate to. [Data: Sources (132)]

## Release Candidate Versions

When upgrading across v2 versions, you should be aware that the go-echarts project releases Release Candidate (RC) versions before standard releases to test minor enhancements. [Data: Entities (2062); Relationships (3122)] If you upgrade your projects across RC versions, you may need to make small adjustments to accommodate these pre-release changes.

## Current Development Status

V2 is the current active version of go-echarts and is under active development on the master branch. [Data: Entities (2060, 2063); Relationships (3119, 3121)] This means that if you do decide to migrate from v1 to v2, you'll be moving to a version that is actively maintained and receiving ongoing improvements.

question: How does go-echarts represent a boolean echarts option whose default value is true?
answer:
# Boolean Option Representation in go-echarts

## Type Definition

Go-echarts represents a boolean echarts option with a default value of `true` using a pointer to bool, defined as the `types.Bool` type [Data: Entities (2074); Sources (133)]. This design choice is necessary because Go's native boolean type cannot distinguish between an explicitly set value and a missing value that should use the default.

## Conversion Function

To facilitate working with this type, go-echarts provides the `opts.Bool()` function, which converts boolean values to the `types.Bool` pointer type [Data: Entities (2070, 2298); Relationships (3134); Sources (133)]. This handy function makes it easy for developers to work with boolean options without manually managing pointers.

## Rationale

This approach addresses a fundamental difference between JavaScript (which echarts uses) and Go. Since echarts is a pure JavaScript library with flexible type handling, go-echarts needed to adapt its type system for Go's stricter typing. By using a pointer to bool, go-echarts can represent three states: `nil` (use default value of true), `true` (explicitly set to true), and `false` (explicitly set to false) [Data: Sources (133)]. This allows go-echarts to accurately generate the echarts-required options while maintaining type safety in Go.

In golang, go-echarts is not feasible to achieve it in a simple way. Besides, some of the options may have default values which may not consistent with go types. Therefore, we change some types following this guideline for now: * If the bool option with default(missing) value `(true)`, define it `*bool`(`types.Bool`) and provide the handy func `opts.Bool()` to do convert easily. * If the option is `string|string array` or `number|number array`, define it in `type array` or `interface{}`. * If the option is a complex struct, define it `interface{}` or providing an usable function, convert it then. JS Function and Formatter String ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- > Formatter string sounds like a DSL for echarts, such as `formatter: '{b0}: {c0}
{b1}: {c1}'` or a pure JS > function. Since go-echarts renders the options to charts pure in go, there is no way to apply JS functions either on echarts options or echarts instance directly. Instead, we provide the ability to insert pure JS function string and some useful functional wrapper api to help users do operations on echarts and echarts instance. The type of those kind of `Function String` is `types.FuncStr`. *When you find the option type is `types.FuncStr`, you should notice it. :)* How to insert the pure JS function --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- * Use `opts.FuncOpts` or `opts.FuncStripCommentsOpts` to create your JS string. * Use `myChart.AddJSFuncStrs()` to add the JS function into your charts. For example: ``` actionWithEchartsInstance := ` let currentIndex = -1; setInterval(function() { const myChart = %MY_ECHARTS%; var dataLen = myChart.getOption().series[0].data.length; myChart.dispatchAction({ type: 'downplay', seriesIndex: 0, dataIndex: currentIndex }); currentIndex = (currentIndex + 1) % dataLen; myChart.dispatchAction({ type: 'highlight', seriesIndex: 0, dataIndex: currentIndex }); myChart.dispatchAction({ type: 'showTip', seriesIndex: 0, dataIndex: currentIndex }); }, 1000); ` pie := charts.NewPie() pie.AddJSFuncStrs(opts.FuncOpts(actionWithEchartsInstance) ``` > BTW: use `const` to define a pure function string can do the builtin convert directly. How to get echarts instance ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Especially, you may notice the special var `%MY_ECHARTS%` in the example above. The `%MY_ECHARTS%` is the placeholder of the `echarts instance` in go-echarts. It will inject each of the real `echarts instance` of the chart into your functions. We believe it could bring more convenient to you when you want to do some advance operates on charts. Normally, you don't need it when you don't need do functions on chart, since go-echarts wants keep it always simple. --- Where to find options you need ===================================================================================== go-echarts' options are almost align to [echarts' official options](https://echarts.apache.org/en/option.html#title). If you want to find the options of your specific charts, all in the echarts options list. And if you find some options go-echarts hasn't supported yet, kindly create a PR or raise an option request. --- Where to find custom echarts resources ===================================================================================================== Currently, we support echarts' version is `v5.4.3` and the compatible version `v4.3` for those 3d charts and customized charts, such as word-cloud. All the resources are hosted in [go-echarts-assets](https://github.com/go-echarts/go-echarts-assets) by go-echarts itself. If you want to use your custom echarts resources. You could find in the [jsdelivr of echarts](https://www.jsdelivr.com/package/npm/echarts) or other CDN providers. Besides, you can set your own assets host as well. We support 2 ways to customize the echarts resources. * Only change the `Asserts Host`, which needs the echarts resources naming `echarts.min.js` * Clean all the preset assets and add custom resources all by yourself. ---

these aspects.

---

Ecosystem of go-echarts
=======================================================================

Welcome to contribute your awesome integration case !!!

This part lists all the ecosystem of go-echarts. Thanks for those great works.

* [`templ`](https://github.com/a-h/templ) A language for writing HTML user interfaces in Go. You can use `go-echarts` as its components.
* [`GoNB`](https://github.com/janpfeifer/gonb) A Go Notebook Kernel for Jupyter. You can run `go-echarts` inside of it smoothly, see [examples](https://janpfeifer.github.io/gonb-echarts/).
* [`insyra`](https://github.com/HazelnutParadise/insyra) A next-generation data analysis library for Golang(`go-echarts` as the main visualization backend).

---

Container of echarts
=======================================================================

A `Container` is used to define a root dom box of echarts instance and how to render charts.
It contains the height, width...etc, more
in [echarts Chart Container](https://echarts.apache.org/handbook/en/concepts/chart-size)

It focuses on the single echarts box instead of the whole pages,
go-echarts follows its rules on each chart level as well.
Obviously, go-echarts needs the HTML page management thing before do echarts stuff also.

Container of go-echarts
=============================================================================

In go-echarts, there have two approaches to manage charts, for single chart and for multi charts.
It has a little different points more than a simple aggregation operation either.
The `Container` is more close to a `HTML` page result in go-echarts.

* On single chart, it only has the single Chart Container with Chart Render.
* On multi charts, it only has the single Page Container with Page Render.

**There is no strict `1:n` relationship between `Chart Container` and `Page Container`.**

We hold the `Charter` (interface for charts) instances in program level for `Chart Container` and `Page Container`
with individual templates.

Chart Container
-------------------------------------------------------------

A Chart Container is made for a single chart.
The templates it required:

* header.tpl
* base.tpl
* chart.tpl

It allows to customize the asserts on JS and CSS, and provides the shortcuts for page settings.
Because it is only one chart which means it is associated with single echarts container also.
Any change only applies to the single chart page, directly and plain.

Page Container
-----------------------------------------------------------

A Page Container is made for multi charts.
The templates it required:

* header.tpl
* base.tpl
* page.tpl

It allows to customize the assets on JS and CSS on page level and charts level.
Because it contains multi charts in one page, it is associated with multi echarts containers also.
There support layout types:

* 'none'
* 'center'
* 'flex'

Any changes on page level should compatible to chart level, otherwise, it may has side effect.

**Attention**

* In `Page Container`, all the config for page related options on chart level will be ignored, such as `PageTitile`.
* If you want to reset Page assets entirely, only clear preset assets on page level might not work,since the charts level's preset assets
  will replenish it。you need clear all the page assets related options in both Page and Charts level.

---

question: How can I save a go-echarts chart as a PNG image?
answer:
# Saving Go-Echarts Charts as PNG Images

## Overview

To save a go-echarts chart as a PNG image, you can use the **snapshot-chromedp** library, which is the currently supported approach for rendering charts to image files [Data: Sources (138); Entities (2173); Relationships (3252, 3268)].

## How It Works

The snapshot-chromedp library uses a headless browser approach to convert your charts into images. Here's the process:

1. **HTML Generation**: The library generates an HTML file containing your rendered chart
2. **Image Capture**: It uses a headless browser to capture the chart as a base64 image via the echarts API
3. **File Output**: The captured image is saved to your specified file path
4. **Cleanup**: By default, the intermediate HTML file is automatically deleted after the image is captured [Data: Sources (138); Entities (2173, 2184); Relationships (3264, 3266)]

## Basic Usage

The simplest way to render a chart to an image is using the `MakeChartSnapshot` function:

```go
render.MakeChartSnapshot(myChart.RenderContent(), "my-chart.png")
```

This seamless function handles the entire process with default settings [Data: Sources (138); Entities (2187); Relationships (3269)].

## Advanced Configuration

For more control over the image generation process, you can use the `SnapshotConfig` structure to customize various aspects:

- **Path and FileName**: Specify where to save the image and what to name it
- **Suffix**: Choose image format (png, jpeg)
- **Quality**: Set the generated image quality via pixelRatio
- **KeepHtml**: Optionally retain the generated HTML file instead of deleting it
- **HtmlPath**: Specify a custom location for keeping the HTML file
- **Timeout**: Configure timeout settings for the rendering process
- **MultiCharts**: Enable this option when rendering multiple charts on a single page, and consider setting a larger quality value [Data: Sources (138); Entities (2173, 3254)]

For complete details and additional configuration options, refer to the [go-echarts/snapshot-chromedp](https://github.com/go-echarts/snapshot-chromedp) repository [Data: Sources (138)].

# Registering a Click Handler on a Go-Echarts Bar Chart

To register a click handler on a go-echarts bar chart, you need to use the `WithEventListeners` function combined with the `event.Listener` struct. Here's how to do it:

## Basic Approach

First, define your JavaScript handler function as a string. Then, pass it to `SetGlobalOptions` using `WithEventListeners` [Data: Sources (135)].

## Implementation Example

Here's a complete example of registering a click handler on a bar chart:

```go
bar := charts.NewBar()
JFunc := `(params) => alert(params.name)`
bar.SetGlobalOptions(
    charts.WithEventListeners(
        event.Listener{
            EventName: "click",
            Handler:   opts.FuncOpts(JFunc),
        },
    )
)
```

## Event.Listener Structure

The `event.Listener` struct has three key fields [Data: Entities (2108); Sources (135)]:

- **EventName**: Specifies the event type, such as `"click"`, `"mouseover"`, etc. [Data: Entities (2108)]
- **Query**: An optional filter for events (e.g., `"'series'"` or `"{ seriesName: 'foo' }"`), allowing you to target specific chart elements [Data: Entities (2108)]
- **Handler**: Contains the JavaScript function string that executes when the event is triggered, formatted as `(params) => {...}` [Data: Entities (2108)]

## Advanced Example with Multiple Listeners

You can register multiple event listeners on the same chart [Data: Sources (135)]:

```go
bar := charts.NewBar()
JFunc := `(params) => alert(params.name)`
bar.SetGlobalOptions(
    charts.WithEventListeners(
        event.Listener{
            EventName: "click",
            Handler:   opts.FuncOpts(JFunc),
        },
        event.Listener{
            EventName: "mouseover",
            Query:     "{ seriesName: 'go-echarts' }",
            Handler:   opts.FuncOpts(JFunc),
        },
    )
)
```

This approach allows you to create interactive bar charts that respond to user interactions like clicks and mouse movements [Data: Sources (135)].

In golang, go-echarts is not feasible to achieve it in a simple way. Besides, some of the options may have default values which may not consistent with go types. Therefore, we change some types following this guideline for now: * If the bool option with default(missing) value `(true)`, define it `*bool`(`types.Bool`) and provide the handy func `opts.Bool()` to do convert easily. * If the option is `string|string array` or `number|number array`, define it in `type array` or `interface{}`. * If the option is a complex struct, define it `interface{}` or providing an usable function, convert it then. JS Function and Formatter String ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- > Formatter string sounds like a DSL for echarts, such as `formatter: '{b0}: {c0}
{b1}: {c1}'` or a pure JS > function. Since go-echarts renders the options to charts pure in go, there is no way to apply JS functions either on echarts options or echarts instance directly. Instead, we provide the ability to insert pure JS function string and some useful functional wrapper api to help users do operations on echarts and echarts instance. The type of those kind of `Function String` is `types.FuncStr`. *When you find the option type is `types.FuncStr`, you should notice it. :)* How to insert the pure JS function --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- * Use `opts.FuncOpts` or `opts.FuncStripCommentsOpts` to create your JS string. * Use `myChart.AddJSFuncStrs()` to add the JS function into your charts. For example: ``` actionWithEchartsInstance := ` let currentIndex = -1; setInterval(function() { const myChart = %MY_ECHARTS%; var dataLen = myChart.getOption().series[0].data.length; myChart.dispatchAction({ type: 'downplay', seriesIndex: 0, dataIndex: currentIndex }); currentIndex = (currentIndex + 1) % dataLen; myChart.dispatchAction({ type: 'highlight', seriesIndex: 0, dataIndex: currentIndex }); myChart.dispatchAction({ type: 'showTip', seriesIndex: 0, dataIndex: currentIndex }); }, 1000); ` pie := charts.NewPie() pie.AddJSFuncStrs(opts.FuncOpts(actionWithEchartsInstance) ``` > BTW: use `const` to define a pure function string can do the builtin convert directly. How to get echarts instance ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Especially, you may notice the special var `%MY_ECHARTS%` in the example above. The `%MY_ECHARTS%` is the placeholder of the `echarts instance` in go-echarts. It will inject each of the real `echarts instance` of the chart into your functions. We believe it could bring more convenient to you when you want to do some advance operates on charts. Normally, you don't need it when you don't need do functions on chart, since go-echarts wants keep it always simple. --- Where to find options you need ===================================================================================== go-echarts' options are almost align to [echarts' official options](https://echarts.apache.org/en/option.html#title). If you want to find the options of your specific charts, all in the echarts options list. And if you find some options go-echarts hasn't supported yet, kindly create a PR or raise an option request. --- Where to find custom echarts resources ===================================================================================================== Currently, we support echarts' version is `v5.4.3` and the compatible version `v4.3` for those 3d charts and customized charts, such as word-cloud. All the resources are hosted in [go-echarts-assets](https://github.com/go-echarts/go-echarts-assets) by go-echarts itself. If you want to use your custom echarts resources. You could find in the [jsdelivr of echarts](https://www.jsdelivr.com/package/npm/echarts) or other CDN providers. Besides, you can set your own assets host as well. We support 2 ways to customize the echarts resources. * Only change the `Asserts Host`, which needs the echarts resources naming `echarts.min.js` * Clean all the preset assets and add custom resources all by yourself. ---

Ecosystem of go-echarts
=======================================================================

Welcome to contribute your awesome integration case !!!

This part lists all the ecosystem of go-echarts. Thanks for those great works.

* [`templ`](https://github.com/a-h/templ) A language for writing HTML user interfaces in Go. You can use `go-echarts` as its components.
* [`GoNB`](https://github.com/janpfeifer/gonb) A Go Notebook Kernel for Jupyter. You can run `go-echarts` inside of it smoothly, see [examples](https://janpfeifer.github.io/gonb-echarts/).
* [`insyra`](https://github.com/HazelnutParadise/insyra) A next-generation data analysis library for Golang(`go-echarts` as the main visualization backend).

---

Container of echarts
=======================================================================

A `Container` is used to define a root dom box of echarts instance and how to render charts.
It contains the height, width...etc, more
in [echarts Chart Container](https://echarts.apache.org/handbook/en/concepts/chart-size)

It focuses on the single echarts box instead of the whole pages,
go-echarts follows its rules on each chart level as well.
Obviously, go-echarts needs the HTML page management thing before do echarts stuff also.

Container of go-echarts
=============================================================================

In go-echarts, there have two approaches to manage charts, for single chart and for multi charts.
It has a little different points more than a simple aggregation operation either.
The `Container` is more close to a `HTML` page result in go-echarts.

* On single chart, it only has the single Chart Container with Chart Render.
* On multi charts, it only has the single Page Container with Page Render.

**There is no strict `1:n` relationship between `Chart Container` and `Page Container`.**

We hold the `Charter` (interface for charts) instances in program level for `Chart Container` and `Page Container`
with individual templates.

Chart Container
-------------------------------------------------------------

A Chart Container is made for a single chart.
The templates it required:

* header.tpl
* base.tpl
* chart.tpl

It allows to customize the asserts on JS and CSS, and provides the shortcuts for page settings.
Because it is only one chart which means it is associated with single echarts container also.
Any change only applies to the single chart page, directly and plain.

Page Container
-----------------------------------------------------------

A Page Container is made for multi charts.
The templates it required:

* header.tpl
* base.tpl
* page.tpl

It allows to customize the assets on JS and CSS on page level and charts level.
Because it contains multi charts in one page, it is associated with multi echarts containers also.
There support layout types:

* 'none'
* 'center'
* 'flex'

Any changes on page level should compatible to chart level, otherwise, it may has side effect.

**Attention**

* In `Page Container`, all the config for page related options on chart level will be ignored, such as `PageTitile`.
* If you want to reset Page assets entirely, only clear preset assets on page level might not work,since the charts level's preset assets
  will replenish it。you need clear all the page assets related options in both Page and Charts level.

question: Which go-echarts function creates a Sankey chart, and which option types define its nodes and links?
answer:
# Creating Sankey Charts in Go-Echarts

## Chart Creation Function

The `charts.NewSankey` function is used to create a new Sankey chart instance in go-echarts [Data: Entities (2239)]. This function initializes a Sankey chart object that can then be configured with nodes, links, and various styling options.

## Node and Link Definition Types

Sankey diagrams in go-echarts use two specific data structure types from the opts package to define their structure:

**SankeyNode** is a data structure that defines the nodes in a Sankey diagram, with a Name attribute that identifies each node [Data: Entities (2224)]. These nodes represent the categories or entities that will appear in the diagram.

**SankeyLink** is a data structure that defines the connections between nodes, with Source, Target, and Value attributes [Data: Entities (2225)]. The Source and Target attributes specify which nodes are connected, while the Value attribute represents the magnitude of the flow between them.

## Practical Implementation

In practice, these types work together within the Sankey chart workflow. After creating a Sankey instance with `charts.NewSankey`, developers populate it by calling `AddSeries` with arrays of `SankeyNode` and `SankeyLink` objects [Data: Sources (142)]. The nodes define the structure of the diagram, while the links define how data flows between those nodes, allowing for clear visualization of relationships and quantities in the data.

question: I render several go-echarts charts on one page and set a PageTitle on each chart, but the title is ignored. Why, and which templates does that page use?
answer:
# Why PageTitle is Ignored on Multi-Chart Pages

When you render multiple go-echarts charts on a single page using a Page Container, the PageTitle configuration set on individual charts is intentionally ignored. This is by design in the go-echarts architecture.

## The Reason for Ignored PageTitle

The PageTitle configuration is a page-level option that only applies when you're working with a single chart in a Chart Container. When you use a Page Container to manage multiple charts on one page, all chart-level page-related configuration options—including PageTitle—are disregarded [Data: Entities (2103); Relationships (3173)]. This design choice prevents conflicts and confusion that could arise from having multiple charts trying to set the same page-level property simultaneously.

## Templates Used by Page Container

A Page Container uses three template files to render your multi-chart page [Data: Entities (2093, 2098, 2099, 2101); Relationships (3162, 3163, 3164)]:

1. **header.tpl** - Provides common header functionality shared across all chart types
2. **base.tpl** - Supplies the base structural template also shared with single-chart pages
3. **page.tpl** - The specialized template specific to multi-chart page rendering

These templates work together to create the complete HTML page structure needed to display multiple charts with proper layout and styling.

## Recommended Approach

If you need to set a title for your multi-chart page, you should configure it at the page level rather than on individual charts. This ensures the title is properly applied to the entire page rather than being ignored at the chart level.

question: If I clear the preset JS and CSS assets on a go-echarts page but the old assets still appear, what went wrong?
answer:
# Clearing Preset Assets in Go-Echarts: Troubleshooting Guide

## The Problem with Page-Level Asset Clearing

If you've cleared the preset JavaScript and CSS assets on your go-echarts page but the old assets still appear, the issue likely stems from how go-echarts manages assets across different container levels. This is a common gotcha when working with multi-chart pages.

## Why Old Assets Persist

The root cause is that go-echarts uses a two-level asset management system. When you have multiple charts on a page, clearing preset assets only at the page level may not be sufficient [Data: Sources (134); Entities (2107); Relationships (3174)]. This is because individual charts maintain their own preset assets at the chart level, and these chart-level assets can replenish the page-level assets even after you've cleared them [Data: Sources (134)].

## The Solution

To properly reset page assets entirely, you need to clear all page-asset-related options at **both the Page level and the Chart level** [Data: Sources (134)]. Simply clearing preset assets on the page level alone won't work if the charts themselves still have their preset assets configured [Data: Sources (134)].

Go-echarts provides specific functions to help with this:

- `ClearPresetAssets()` - clears both preset JS and CSS static assets [Data: Entities (2190); Relationships (3273)]
- `ClearPresetJSAssets()` - clears only preset JavaScript assets [Data: Entities (2191); Relationships (3274)]
- `ClearPresetCSSAssets()` - clears only preset CSS assets [Data: Entities (2192); Relationships (3275)]

Make sure to apply these clearing operations consistently across all charts in your page container to prevent the chart-level preset assets from replenishing the page-level assets.

* page.tpl

question: What does Docsify's relativePath option do, and what is its default?
answer:
# Docsify's relativePath Option

## Purpose

The `relativePath` option is a boolean configuration setting in Docsify that controls how links within markdown files are resolved [Data: Entities (2445); Relationships (3711)]. When enabled, it makes links relative to the current context instead of using absolute paths [Data: Entities (2445)].

## Default Value

The default value for `relativePath` is `false`, meaning relative path resolution is disabled by default [Data: Sources (155)].

## How It Works

When `relativePath` is set to `true`, links are resolved relative to the current URL path. For example, with a directory structure containing nested folders like `docs/zh-cn/config/`, a link to `guide.md` from the path `http://domain.com/zh-cn/README` would resolve to `http://domain.com/zh-cn/guide` rather than an absolute path [Data: Sources (155)].

This is particularly useful for documentation sites with multiple language versions or nested directory structures, as it allows markdown files to use relative links that work correctly regardless of where they're accessed from within the site [Data: Sources (155)].

## Configuration

To enable relative path resolution, you would configure it in the `window.$docsify` object:

```javascript
window.$docsify = {
  relativePath: true,
};
```

-------------------------------------------

Configure the URL format that the paths of your site will use.

* Type: `String`

window.$docsify = {

For statically-deployed sites (f.e. on GitHub Pages) hash-based routing is
simpler to set up. For websites that can re-write URLs, the history-based format
is better (especially for search-engine optimization, hash-based routing is not
so search-engine friendly)

Hash-based routing means all URL paths will be prefixed with `/#/` in the
address bar. This is a trick that allows the site to load `/index.html`, then it
uses the path that follows the `#` to determine what markdown files to load. For
example, a complete hash-based URL may look like this:
`https://example.com/#/path/to/page`. The browser will actually load
`https://example.com` (assuming your static server serves
`index.html` by default, as most do), and then the Docsify JavaScript code will
look at the `/#/...` and determine the markdown file to load and render.
Additionally, when clicking on a link, the Docsify router will change the
content after the hash dynamically. The value of `location.pathname` will still be
`/` no matter what. The parts of a hash path are *not* sent to the server when
visiting such a URL in a browser.

On the other hand, history-based routing means the Docsify JavaScript will use
the [History API](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/History_API)
to dynamically change the URL without using a `#`. This means that all URLs will
be considered "real" by search engines, and the full path will be sent to the
server when visiting the URL in your browser. For example, a URL may look like
`https://example.com/path/to/page`. The browser will try to load that full URL
directly from the server, not just `https://example.com`. The upside of this is
that these types of URLs are much more friendly for search engines, and can be
indexed (yay!). The downside, however, is that your server, or the place where
you host your site files, has to be able to handle these URLs. Various static

------------------------------------

In order to have a sidebar, you can create your own `_sidebar.md` (see [this documentation's sidebar](https://github.com/docsifyjs/docsify/blob/main/docs/_sidebar.md) for an example):

First, you need to set `loadSidebar` to **true**. Details are available in the [configuration paragraph](#/configuration?id=loadsidebar).

```
<!-- index.html -->

<script>
  window.$docsify = {
    loadSidebar: true,
  };
</script>
<script src="//cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/docsify@5/dist/docsify.min.js"></script>
```

Create the `_sidebar.md`:

```
<!-- docs/_sidebar.md -->

- [Home](/)
- [Page 1](page-1.md)
```

To create section headers:

```
<!-- docs/_sidebar.md -->

- Section Header 1

  - [Home](/)
  - [Page 1](page-1.md)

- Section Header 2

  - [Page 2](page-2.md)
  - [Page 3](page-3.md)
```

You need to create a `.nojekyll` in `./docs` to prevent GitHub Pages from ignoring files that begin with an underscore.

Docsify only looks for `_sidebar.md` in the current folder, and uses that, otherwise it falls back to the one configured using `window.$docsify.loadSidebar` config.

Example file structure:

```
└── docs/
    ├── _sidebar.md
    ├── index.md
    ├── getting-started.md
    └── running-services.md
```

Nested Sidebars
----------------------------------------------------

You may want the sidebar to update after navigation to reflect the current directory. This can be done by adding a `_sidebar.md` file to each folder.

`_sidebar.md` is loaded from each level directory. If the current directory doesn't have `_sidebar.md`, it will fall back to the parent directory. If, for example, the current path is `/guide/quick-start`, the `_sidebar.md` will be loaded from `/guide/_sidebar.md`.

You can specify `alias` to avoid unnecessary fallback.

```
<script>
  window.$docsify = {
    loadSidebar: true,
    alias: {
      '/.*/_sidebar.md': '/_sidebar.md',
    },
  };
</script>
```

You can create a `README.md` file in a subdirectory to use it as the landing page for the route.

Set Page Titles from Sidebar Selection
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

A page's `title` tag is generated from the *selected* sidebar item name. For better SEO, you can customize the title by specifying a string after the filename.

```
<!-- docs/_sidebar.md -->

- [Home](/)
- [Guide](guide.md 'The greatest guide in the world')
```

Table of Contents
--------------------------------------------------------

Once you've created `_sidebar.md`, the sidebar content is automatically generated based on the headers in the markdown files.

A custom sidebar can also automatically generate a table of contents by setting a `subMaxLevel`, compare [subMaxLevel configuration](#/configuration?id=submaxlevel).

```
<!-- index.html -->

<script>
  window.$docsify = {
    loadSidebar: true,
    subMaxLevel: 2,
  };
</script>
<script src="//cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/docsify@5/dist/docsify.min.js"></script>
```

Ignoring Subheaders
------------------------------------------------------------

When `subMaxLevel` is set, each header is automatically added to the table of contents by default. If you want to ignore a specific header, add `<!-- {docsify-ignore} -->` to it.

```
# Getting Started

## Header <!-- {docsify-ignore} -->

This header won't appear in the sidebar table of contents.
```

To ignore all headers on a specific page, you can use `<!-- {docsify-ignore-all} -->` on the first header of the page.

```
# Getting Started <!-- {docsify-ignore-all} -->

## Header

This header won't appear in the sidebar table of contents.
```

Both `<!-- {docsify-ignore} -->` and `<!-- {docsify-ignore-all} -->` will not be rendered on the page when used.

And the `{docsify-ignore}` and `{docsify-ignore-all}` can do the samething as well.

# Creating a Liquid Fill Chart with Wave Animation in Go-Echarts

## Overview

To create a liquid fill chart with wave animation in go-echarts, you need to use the `NewLiquid` constructor function and configure the wave animation settings through the chart options [Data: Entities (2292)].

## Basic Steps

### 1. Create a Liquid Chart Instance

Start by creating a new Liquid chart using the `NewLiquid` function [Data: Entities (2292); Relationships (3471)]:

```go
liquid := charts.NewLiquid()
```

### 2. Set Global Options

Configure the chart's global options, such as the title, using `SetGlobalOptions` [Data: Relationships (3479)]:

```go
liquid.SetGlobalOptions(
    charts.WithTitleOpts(opts.Title{
        Title: "basic liquid example",
    }),
)
```

### 3. Add Data Series

Add your data to the chart using `AddSeries` [Data: Relationships (3487)]. The data should be provided as liquid data items:

```go
liquid.AddSeries("liquid", genLiquidItems([]float32{0.3, 0.4, 0.5}))
```

### 4. Enable Wave Animation

Configure the series options with `SetSeriesOptions` to enable wave animation [Data: Relationships (3495)]. Use `WithLiquidChartOpts` to set the `IsWaveAnimation` property to `true` [Data: Relationships (3506, 3507)]:

```go
.SetSeriesOptions(
    charts.WithLiquidChartOpts(opts.LiquidChart{
        IsWaveAnimation: opts.Bool(true),
    }),
)
```

## Complete Example

Here's a complete example that demonstrates creating a liquid chart with wave animation enabled [Data: Sources (145, 146)]:

```go
func liquidBase() *charts.Liquid {
    liquid := charts.NewLiquid()
    liquid.SetGlobalOptions(
        charts.WithTitleOpts(opts.Title{
            Title: "basic liquid example",
        }),
    )

    liquid.AddSeries("liquid", genLiquidItems([]float32{0.3, 0.4, 0.5})).
        SetSeriesOptions(
            charts.WithLiquidChartOpts(opts.LiquidChart{
                IsWaveAnimation: opts.Bool(true),
            }),
        )
    return liquid
}
```

## Additional Configuration Options

The `WithLiquidChartOpts` function supports additional configuration options beyond wave animation [Data: Entities (2294)]. For example, you can customize the chart shape [Data: Relationships (3508)]:

```go
charts.WithLiquidChartOpts(opts.LiquidChart{
    IsWaveAnimation: opts.Bool(true),
    Shape:           "diamond",  // or "pin", "arrow", "triangle"
})
```

## Rendering the Chart

To render your liquid chart to an HTML file, use the `Render` method [Data: Relationships (3513, 3514)]:

```go
f, err := os.Create("liquid.html")
if err != nil {
    panic(err)
}
page.Render(io.MultiWriter(f))
```

Container of echarts
=======================================================================

A `Container` is used to define a root dom box of echarts instance and how to render charts.
It contains the height, width...etc, more
in [echarts Chart Container](https://echarts.apache.org/handbook/en/concepts/chart-size)

It focuses on the single echarts box instead of the whole pages,
go-echarts follows its rules on each chart level as well.
Obviously, go-echarts needs the HTML page management thing before do echarts stuff also.

Container of go-echarts
=============================================================================

In go-echarts, there have two approaches to manage charts, for single chart and for multi charts.
It has a little different points more than a simple aggregation operation either.
The `Container` is more close to a `HTML` page result in go-echarts.

* On single chart, it only has the single Chart Container with Chart Render.
* On multi charts, it only has the single Page Container with Page Render.

**There is no strict `1:n` relationship between `Chart Container` and `Page Container`.**

We hold the `Charter` (interface for charts) instances in program level for `Chart Container` and `Page Container`
with individual templates.

Chart Container
-------------------------------------------------------------

A Chart Container is made for a single chart.
The templates it required:

* header.tpl
* base.tpl
* chart.tpl

It allows to customize the asserts on JS and CSS, and provides the shortcuts for page settings.
Because it is only one chart which means it is associated with single echarts container also.
Any change only applies to the single chart page, directly and plain.

Page Container
-----------------------------------------------------------

A Page Container is made for multi charts.
The templates it required:

* header.tpl
* base.tpl
* page.tpl

It allows to customize the assets on JS and CSS on page level and charts level.
Because it contains multi charts in one page, it is associated with multi echarts containers also.
There support layout types:

* 'none'
* 'center'
* 'flex'

Any changes on page level should compatible to chart level, otherwise, it may has side effect.

**Attention**

* In `Page Container`, all the config for page related options on chart level will be ignored, such as `PageTitile`.
* If you want to reset Page assets entirely, only clear preset assets on page level might not work,since the charts level's preset assets
  will replenish it。you need clear all the page assets related options in both Page and Charts level.
